frequency_question: How often do major, highly contested structural energy permitting or grid reform bills successfully navigate all legislative veto points and pass into law within a single congressional session?
membership_rule: Includes major omnibus energy, grid, or permitting reform bills that faced significant cross-party or intra-party structural friction; excludes minor, uncontested, or unanimous technical corrections bills.

cases.name: Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007
American Clean Energy and Security Act (Waxman-Markey)
Energy Act of 2020 (as part of omnibus)

coverage_note: 7 major attempts identified representing the class of contested energy/permitting legislative pushes over two decades.
known_gaps: Some minor standalone committee-level permitting reforms that stalled quietly are omitted as they do not match the scale of 'comprehensive energy permitting reform'.
validity_reason: Polarization dynamics and the procedural rules of the Senate (like the filibuster) remain stable across multiple recent congressional sessions.
